outlooksByWeek.2: Christian McCaffrey heads into a Week 2 matchup against Miami with perhaps a bit less pressure to carry the 49ers' offense. Whereas McCaffrey led the NFL with 413 touches last season, he logged a modest 15 in last Thursday's Week 1 win over the Rams. Rookie Kaelon Black actually got more carries (14) than McCaffrey (10), though McCaffrey was still productive with 68 rushing yards along with 20 receiving yards on five catches. McCaffrey could feast upon a Dolphins defense that allowed Ashton Jeanty to accumulate 147 total yards and two touchdowns in a season-opening loss to Las Vegas.
outlooksByWeek.3: Christian McCaffrey will look to once again show off his dual-threat skill set when the 49ers host the Cardinals in Week 3. McCaffrey is coming off a productive game against the Dolphins,  totaling 66 yards (23 rushing, 43 receiving) and getting into the end zone twice. The veteran RB has been ceding a fair amount of carries to rookie No. 2 RB Kaelon Black so far this season, but McCaffrey's work as a receiver (nine catches for 63 yards through two contests) has remained a key part of his game. Arizona has been middle-of-the-pack against running backs so far, yielding an average of 14.0 fantasy points per game to the position.
outlooksByWeek.4: Christian McCaffrey is coming off his best game of the campaign heading into San Francisco's Week 4 tilt versus the Broncos. McCaffrey compiled season-high marks with 75 rushing yards and 116 total yards in Sunday's win against Arizona while scoring his third TD of 2026. His 15 carries were also his most so far this season, as the 49ers appear to be pulling back on his workload a bit after he led the NFL with 413 touches last year. McCaffrey could find room to run on Denver, as the Broncos have so far given up the second-most rushing yards to RBs (129.7 per game) this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Christian McCaffrey will look to reach the end zone again for San Francisco in a Week 5 NFC West clash against the Seahawks. McCaffrey has scored at least one touchdown in three straight games and has four rushing TDs on the season. The scoring has helped keep his fantasy value high despite the fact that he's averaging a modest 16.5 touches per game so far after leading the NFL with 24.3 touches per game last season. Seattle has yielded just 3.35 yards per carry and one total rushing touchdown to running backs this season, but they've been more vulnerable through the air, allowing two receiving scores and an 88.5% catch rate to the position.

player.seasonOutlook: McCaffrey is back for his fifth season with the 49ers after a bounce-back 2025 campaign in which he led all running backs in snaps, routes, touches, targets, receptions, receiving yards, receiving touchdowns and fantasy points. McCaffrey's rushing efficiency wasn't great (3.86 yards per carry), and he's entering his age-30 season after handling 450 touches (including the playoffs) in 2025. The history of overworked backs suggests we should expect a step back in 2026, but CMC is a unicorn, and the combination of his skill set and hefty usage in Kyle Shanahan's offense suggests he can overcome history. There's obvious risk here, but McCaffrey will be an elite option whenever he's on the field.

outlooksByWeek.2: Derrick Henry and the Ravens play host to the Saints for their 2026 home opener in Week 2. Henry rambled for 144 yards and three TDs on 24 carries and caught his only target for 19 yards in Baltimore's 41-23 victory. Next up is a Saints defense that surrendered 165 yards and two TDs on the ground to Jahmyr Gibbs and the Lions. Henry has tallied 16 rushing TDs in consecutive years, and he's nearly a quarter of the way there already after just one game.
outlooksByWeek.3: Derrick Henry and the Ravens travel to Texas to battle the Cowboys in Week 3. In Baltimore's Week 2 loss, Henry rushed 16 times for 68 yards and one score, and he caught all three targets for another 19 yards. He accounted for 16 of 18 carries out of the backfield, and he'll continue earning a massive workload on the ground in order to take pressure off Lamar Jackson. Henry faces a Dallas defense that ranks 25th in fantasy points per game (25.9) and 27th in rushing yards allowed to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Derrick Henry and the Ravens return from Brazil to host the winless Titans in Week 4. He tallied 26 carries for 89 yards and two TDs and caught his only target for no gain during Baltimore's 34-31 last-second victory in Week 3 over Dallas. Tennessee's defense ranks 17th in fantasy points allowed (20.7) to RBs after giving up 138 rushing yards to the Giants. Henry will handle his usual workhorse role and could benefit from a positive game script versus a Titans team that ranks third in fewest points allowed per contest, at 12.3.
outlooksByWeek.5: Derrick Henry and the Ravens are on the road for a Week 5 clash against the Falcons. He tallied 23 carries for 73 yards and one touchdown while catching both of his targets for six yards during Baltimore's Week 4 victory. Henry notched his seventh rushing TD of the season and now has at least one score in all four outings. With Lamar Jackson's (ankle) status up in the air, Henry should continue to be the focal point of the Ravens' offense versus Atlanta's ninth-ranked defense in fantasy points allowed (17.9) per game to RBs.

player.seasonOutlook: Henry continues to defy the odds, playing at a high level despite now entering his age-32 season. In 2025, he finished exactly second in the NFL in rushing yards for the fourth season in a row, and his 24 carries inside the 5-yard line were easily the most in the league. Henry leads the NFL in carries inside the 5-yard line (42) and is second in touchdowns (34) since joining Baltimore prior to the 2024 season, and he hasn't finished lower than eighth among RBs in touchdowns since 2017. Henry continues to run at a high level (his 5.20 yards per carry last season ranked fifth among qualified backs), but he's still a nonfactor as a receiver (outside the top 45 backs in targets, catches and yards last season). He remains a featured rusher in a terrific offense and is well positioned for his fifth consecutive top-eight fantasy campaign.

outlooksByWeek.2: Davante Adams will look to get going when the Rams face the Giants in Week 2. Adams was held to a 3-26-0 receiving line versus San Francisco in Week 1, though the Rams' offense as a whole was held in check. Adams did draw the second-most targets (six) among Los Angeles pass catchers, as he continued to draw QB Matthew Stafford's attention more than any other player besides star Puka Nacua (nine targets). The Giants largely held Dallas' passing game in check during a Week 1 win, with no Cowboys pass catcher logging more than five receptions or 44 yards.
outlooksByWeek.3: Davante Adams is coming off an explosive Monday Night Football performance heading into the Rams' Week 3 matchup versus Denver. With Puka Nacua sidelined by a hip injury, Adams starred Monday against the Giants, posting a massive 10-195-2 line. Nacua's status for Week 3 is up in the air, and Adams would logically stand to be Matthew Stafford's top target again if Nacua can't suit up. However, Denver is a tough matchup, as the Broncos have yielded just 6.55 yards per target to wideouts this season (fifth-best in the NFL).
outlooksByWeek.4: Davante Adams has looked resurgent of late ahead of the Rams' Week 4 tilt against the Eagles. With Puka Nacua (hip) sidelined the past two weeks, Adams has gone off for 15 catches, 332 yards and two touchdowns. However, Nacua has a chance to return to action against Philadelphia, which would potentially result in Adams seeing less attention from QB Matthew Stafford. With that said, both wideouts could feast against an Eagles defense that ranks in the bottom half of the league by giving up an average of 157.7 receiving yards per game to WRs this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Davante Adams is coming off a quiet performance as the Rams prepare to host the Bills in Week 5. Against Philadelphia in Week 4, Adams was held to four catches for 32 yards. That was a substantial downturn after Adams averaged 7.5 catches and 166 yards over the previous two contests, though he still got a healthy nine targets against the Eagles. It has to be mentioned that star wideout Puka Nacua returned to action in Week 4 and posted a 9-125-0 line, while Adams' big performances the previous two weeks took place in games Nacua missed due to injury. Both WRs could find success against the Bills, who have allowed the fourth-most receiving yards to wideouts this year.

player.seasonOutlook: Adams' first season in Los Angeles was a success, as the veteran led the wide receiver position in touchdowns for the third time in the past six seasons. His 27 end zone targets were nine more than any other player and he now sits second in that category (148) and in TDs from scrimmage (117) since entering the league in 2014. Adams' ninth-place finish in fantasy PPG marked his ninth top-10 in his past 10 seasons. Now 33 years old, he isn't targeted as much as in years past (24% target share in 2025 was his lowest since 2016), but he's the clear No. 2 behind Puka Nacua in the Rams' elite, Matthew Stafford-led offense. Adams' heavy usage near the goal line helps cement him as a fine fantasy WR2.

outlooksByWeek.2: George Kittle had a quiet season opener but will look to increase his production when San Francisco faces the Dolphins in Week 2. Kittle tallied a modest two catches (on five targets) for 12 yards in last Thursday's win over the Rams. That was his first game back after tearing his Achilles in January, which may have been a factor in his receiving line following below his usual standards. Miami allowed Raiders tight end Michael Mayer to record six catches in Week 1, suggesting that Kittle could find room to operate against the Dolphins defense.
outlooksByWeek.3: George Kittle will look to build upon Sunday's strong performance when San Francisco hosts the Cardinals in Week 3. In just his second regular-season game since tearing his Achilles in January, Kittle led the 49ers with 80 receiving yards on four catches with one touchdown Sunday in a win over Miami. The veteran tight end remains a key target for QB Brock Purdy, and Kittle's importance in the passing game could be even more elevated with WRs Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and Mike Evans (hip) both managing injuries. Through two weeks, Arizona has allowed tight ends to catch all 10 of their targets for 105 yards.
outlooksByWeek.4: George Kittle enters San Francisco's Week 4 game against Denver as one of the hottest tight ends in the league. Following a quiet season opener in Australia, Kittle has put up 10 catches for 162 yards and three touchdowns over the subsequent two weeks. He's caught all but one of his 11 targets during that span, as he has been clicking very well with QB Brock Purdy. Kittle could continue rolling against a Broncos defense that has given up the eighth-most receiving yards (199) to tight ends so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: George Kittle could again be a key component of San Francisco's offense in Week 5 against Seattle. Kittle has scored a touchdown in three straight games, and he got into the end zone on a game-sealing 56-yard reception in Week 4 versus the Broncos. The veteran tight end enters the clash against Seattle with 244 receiving yards on the season, third-most among NFL tight ends. With that said, the Seahawks' defense has given up the fourth-fewest receiving yards to tight ends, so Kittle has his work cut out for him in Week 5.

player.seasonOutlook: Kittle is undoubtedly among the best tight ends in the NFL and fantasy, but he simply can't dodge the injury bug. The 2017 fifth-round pick has played one full season (2018) and tore an Achilles in the team's wild-card victory after missing six regular-season games last season. Kittle may be ready for Week 1 and isn't expected to miss more than a game or two, though he's now 32 years old and might not be his usual, dominant self even when he returns. Kittle has finished sixth or better in fantasy PPG in each of the past eight seasons (including first in 2024), so his upside makes him worth a late-round flier.

outlooksByWeek.2: Aaron Jones is primed to lead Minnesota's backfield in Week 2 at Chicago. Jones (29 of 65 offensive snaps) and Jordan Mason (30 snaps) had a near-even split of the backfield reps in Week 1, but Mason led the ground attack with 59 yards and a touchdown on 15 carries. Jones still remained heavily involved, as he logged 12 rushes for 40 yards and one touchdown. This week and beyond, Jones will be set to lead the backfield with Mason on IR for a thumb injury. Jones will look to make the most of his likely increased opportunities against a Bears defense that allowed 33.7 PPR points to Panthers running backs in Week 1.
outlooksByWeek.3: Aaron Jones should continue to have a high-usage role as the Vikings travel to Tampa Bay in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 2 with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 23 times for 105 yards. The veteran running back should continue to have a huge role in the coming weeks, while questions remain with the passing game under returning quarterback Kyler Murray. Jones will face a Buccaneers defense that's allowed a middle-of-the-pack 19.5 PPR points per game to RBs.
outlooksByWeek.4: Aaron Jones should remain a high-volume option as the Vikings play Miami in Week 3. Jones saw a big workload in Week 3 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 17 times for 58 yards and recording five catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield doesn't look to be changing with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Miami defense that's allowed the most fantasy points per game (32.9) to running backs so far this season.
outlooksByWeek.5: Aaron Jones will remain a high-usage option as the Vikings travel to New Orleans in Week 5. Jones saw a big workload in Week 4 once again with Jordan Mason (thumb) on IR, rushing the ball 20 times for 94 yards and recording four catches for 34 yards. The veteran running back's high share in the backfield shouldn't change with Mason out another week, even with DeeJay Dallas and Demond Claiborne fighting for touches. Jones will face a Saints defense that's ranked middle-of-the-pack versus fantasy RBs this campaign.

player.seasonOutlook: Jones is back for a third season in Minnesota after an injury-plagued 2025 campaign limited him to 747 yards (his fewest since his rookie season in 2017) and three touchdowns in 12 games. Jones remained fairly busy (11.0 carries and 3.4 targets per game) but didn't perform well, ranking dead last among 65 backs with 50-plus carries in forced missed tackle rate and elusive rating, per PFF. Jones failed to record a single top-10 fantasy outing. Now 31 years old, Jones remains a starter and will get some run, but he's well past his prime and unlikely to return to consistent fantasy output. Jones is best valued as a bench player with occasional flex appeal.
